title: JUBAKU: An Adversarial Benchmark for Exposing Culturally Grounded Stereotypes in Japanese LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM selections in adversarially constructed binary-choice Japanese dialogue scenarios designed to trigger culturally grounded stereotypes across domains like food and drink, emotions and values, and basic actions.
Binary-choice dialogue response selection evaluating stereotypes related to traditional divisions of labor and academic field associations (e.g., STEM vs. Arts).
Binary-choice dialogue response selection evaluating stereotypes concerning Japanese adherence to Shinto and Buddhist traditions versus other world religions.
Binary-choice dialogue response selection evaluating stereotypes regarding indigenous groups in Japan, such as the Ainu and Ryukyuans.
Binary-choice dialogue response selection evaluating stereotypes related to academic ranking, university brands, and educational backgrounds.
Binary-choice dialogue response selection evaluating stereotypes regarding race, such as assumptions about the language proficiencies and origins of foreign students or workers in Japan.
Binary-choice dialogue response selection evaluating stereotypes about Japanese prefectures, including disparities between the Tokyo metropolitan area and rural regions, local food, and dialects.
Binary-choice dialogue response selection evaluating stereotypes related to Japanese naming conventions, unusual kanji readings ('Kira-kira' names), and names of naturalized individuals.
